model: within-transect fixed effects with cyclic survey-day and log sampled-point-count adjustment; node bootstrap

lower_tampa_bay.interpretation: Long-term compositional reorganization is consistent with increasing Halodule frequency while Thalassia and Syringodium decline quantitatively.

old_tampa_bay.community_replacement: No strong monotone Halodule/Syringodium replacement detected in frequency/cover; the stronger focal signal remains Thalassia blade-length and shoot-density decline.

middle_tampa_bay.community_pattern: Thalassia and Syringodium frequency changes are positively coupled rather than compensatory.

claim_boundary: Long-term opposing species slopes are consistent with community reorganization but do not prove competition or replacement mechanism.
Year-to-year correlations are exploratory and are not corrected for multiple testing.
Braun-Blanquet cover is an ordinal abundance index rather than percent cover.
